candidates.source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) — Členové / Members registry
candidates.why_relevant: Server-rendered roster of ČBA member banks — the cheapest near-complete enumeration of licensed banks and foreign bank branches operating in CZ, including building societies (ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna, Stavební spořitelna ČS) and state banks (ČEB, Národní rozvojová banka). Observed ~33 entries incl. Air Bank, AS Inbank odštěpný závod, Banka CREDITAS, Bank of China (CEE), BNP Paribas pobočka, Citibank Europe, COMMERZBANK pobočka Praha, Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, Deutsche Bank Filiale Prag, Fio banka, HSBC Continental Europe, ICBC Prague Branch, ING Bank N.V., J&T BANKA, Komerční banka, mBank organizační složka, MONETA Money Bank, Oberbank AG, Partners Banka, PKO BP Czech Branch, PPF banka, Raiffeisenbank, TRINITY BANK, UniCredit Bank CZ&SK, VÚB pobočka Praha. Each name is a seed for A1 disclosure/IR/annual-report tracking. An English mirror exists at /about-us/members.
candidates.legal_status: public website; robots.txt allows this path (only /api/, /cba_online/, /journal_files_storage/ are disallowed)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Plain HTTP GET + HTML parse; member names appear in the static server-rendered HTML (no JS needed). Poll monthly and diff the roster to catch entries/exits, M&A and branch conversions. Mirror the /about-us/members English page for name normalisation.

candidates.source_name: ČBA Monitor — banking sector & macro statistics portal
candidates.why_relevant: ČBA's dedicated statistics/analysis property, distinct from the main association site. Publishes headline sector aggregates (observed: banking sector assets ~11,911 bn CZK, sector headcount 37,919, 43 banks by size band, sector profits), macro indicators, credit and deposit series, property prices, the ČBA macroeconomic forecast (ČBA Prognóza) and economist commentary. This is the single best free aggregated view of the Czech banking sector's size and direction, and it names the bank economists who front it — useful for A1 earnings/disclosure context and for sourcing quotable sector baselines.
candidates.legal_status: public website, no paywall observed
candidates.suggested_collection_method: HTTP GET + HTML parse of /kategorie/* index pages and /aktuality/* items; content is server-rendered. Category endpoints observed: /kategorie/ekonomika, /kategorie/bankovni-sektor, /kategorie/cba-hypomonitor, /kategorie/cba-prognoza, /kategorie/ceny-nemovitosti. Monthly cadence; check the /en mirror for English titles.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Outbound link from cbaonline.cz primary navigation

candidates.source_name: ČBA Hypomonitor — mortgage market monthly series
candidates.why_relevant: The ČBA Hypomonitor is the de-facto reference series for Czech mortgage volumes and average mortgage rates, compiled from member-bank submissions and released monthly with a press release. It is the most frequently cited private-sector banking dataset in CZ media and is the cleanest recurring datapoint tying individual banks' retail lending momentum to sector totals — high value for A1 earnings and disclosure triangulation.
candidates.legal_status: public website
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly scheduled HTTP GET of the category index, then fetch each new /aktuality/cba-hypomonitor-* item; parse headline rate and volume figures from the article body. Slug pattern observed to embed the rate (e.g. '...se-stale-nizkou-sazbou-452').
candidates.discovered_via_method: Category enumeration on cbamonitor.cz

candidates.source_name: ČBA — Výroční zprávy (annual reports archive)
candidates.why_relevant: Archive of ČBA annual reports as PDFs, with publication dates observed spanning 2011 through 2026-05-26 — sixteen editions. Association annual reports summarise the year's sector aggregates, regulatory files the association fought, working-group output and the member roster as of that year, which makes them the best retrospective series for reconstructing how the Czech banking sector's structure and agenda changed over time.
candidates.access_status: open (index page); PDF binaries sit under a robots-disallowed storage path
candidates.legal_status: Public documents, but note robots.txt Disallow: /journal_files_storage/ — the 'Zobrazit PDF' links resolve into that storage area. Respect robots for automated crawling; fetch PDFs manually or seek permission.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Parse the index page for the dated rows (dates render server-side; the PDF hrefs are injected client-side). Use a headless browser to resolve each 'Zobrazit PDF' target, or contact ČBA press office for a document set. Do NOT bulk-crawl /journal_files_storage/ — it is robots-disallowed.
candidates.discovered_via_method: sitemap.xml enumeration on cbaonline.cz
candidates.observed_blocker: robots.txt disallows /journal_files_storage/ where report PDFs appear to be stored; index page itself is open

candidates.source_name: ČBA — Zpravodajský servis / články (news & commentary stream)
candidates.why_relevant: ČBA's article stream (/clanky/*) carries association press releases, macro commentary, consumer-protection and cyber-security campaigns, and survey write-ups. The sitemap exposes 2,838 URLs of which 704 are /clanky/ items — a complete, crawlable back-catalogue that the JS-rendered front page hides. This is the practical entry point for ČBA press-release monitoring given the site's client-side navigation.
candidates.legal_status: public website; sitemap explicitly advertised in robots.txt
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch sitemap.xml (~1.05 MB), filter loc values matching '/clanky/', use <lastmod> and changefreq for incremental polling, then GET each article. Preferred over scraping the front page, which is client-rendered and returns an empty body to plain HTTP clients.
candidates.discovered_via_method: robots.txt -> sitemap.xml discovery after the rendered homepage yielded only 7 nav links

candidates.source_name: ČBA — Slovník bankovních pojmů (Czech banking terminology glossary)
candidates.why_relevant: The bulk of ČBA's sitemap (roughly 2,100 of 2,838 URLs) is a one-term-per-page Czech banking glossary covering everything from 'zúčtovací systém' and 'zaknihovaný cenný papír' to 'zpráva auditora' and 'zlatá kreditní karta'. For a source-scouting workstream this is a ready-made, authoritative cs<->en terminology corpus for building the local-language query glossary that all other cells depend on — an indirect but high-leverage asset.
candidates.legal_status: public website; reuse of definitions verbatim would be a copyright question — extract terms, not text
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off harvest of sitemap loc slugs (they are the Czech terms themselves) plus the hreflang alternates, which give the ČBA-sanctioned English equivalents. Extract term pairs only; do not republish definition text.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Frequency analysis of sitemap.xml path segments

candidates.source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) — card market statistics
candidates.why_relevant: SBK is the Czech bank card association and this page is the single richest free source on the Czech cards market: downloadable quarterly and full-year card statistics with a year grid running from 2001 to 2026, plus chart series for number of payment cards, cashless transaction counts and volumes, ATM withdrawals, cashback at merchants, e-shop transactions and the merchant-payments-vs-ATM-withdrawal ratio. Critically it also publishes the roster of contributing institutions and a dated changelog of who stopped contributing and why — an implicit, auditable record of Czech card-market exits and consolidations (Zuno into Raiffeisenbank 2017, CCS 2022, Sberbank 04/2022, Diners Club 10/2022, Cofidis 10/2022, Equa Bank into Raiffeisenbank 11/2022, Hello Bank 04/2023, Citibank 01/2024).
candidates.legal_status: public website, no login for the summary tables; note the site is plain HTTP with an HTTPS redirect shim
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Static HTML parse of the year/quarter download grid, then fetch each linked statistics file. Legacy hand-built site (Windows-1250/ISO-8859-2 encoding — decode explicitly, UTF-8 assumptions mangle Czech diacritics). Also scrape the contributor list and the dated exclusion notes as a market-exit event log. Quarterly cadence.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Root bankovnikarty.cz returned a 138-byte META-refresh shim; followed the refresh target to the real site, then link-graph walk
queries_used: Sdružení pro bankovní karty členové statistiky karet tisková zpráva

candidates.why_relevant: Trade magazine for the Czech card/payments community, running since 2003 and clearly co-located with SBK (identical site framework, shared news items, cross-links). Conference agendas and speaker lists are among the cheapest ways to learn which executives own which payments initiatives, which vendors are selling into Czech banks, and what roadmap items get disclosed off the record before they reach an annual report. candidates.why_relevant: A distinct sector association — the Czech factoring companies' association — whose quarterly and annual factoring market statistics are published through the ČLFA site. Observed series run at least 2023-2026 with quarterly granularity (1. čtvrtletí / 1. pololetí / 1.-3. čtvrtletí / rok). Factoring turnover is a leading indicator of SME working-capital stress and of bank-vs-non-bank share shift, and this is the only free consolidated Czech factoring series found.
candidates.legal_status: public website

The site also carries annual reports (cs and an 'annual-report' English variant), plus 'Stanoviska ČLFA' position papers that reveal the association's regulatory lobbying agenda — a good early-warning channel for legislation affecting non-bank credit.

candidates.source_name: Česká fintech asociace / Czech Fintech Association (ČEFTAS) — Členové

Its members page distinguishes 'řádní členové' (full members offering fintech solutions) from 'přidružení členové' (ecosystem supporters), and also lists partner organisations and media/conference partners — three separate enumerations in one page. This is the primary map of the Czech fintech actor set, which is otherwise poorly covered by bank-centric registries. Leadership observed to include executives from Twisto, EasyChange Group and Budget Bakers; the association itself is a member of AMSP ČR, the Czech Chamber of Commerce and the European Digital Finance Association.

candidates.source_name: Asociace pro elektronickou komerci (APEK) — Seznam členů
candidates.why_relevant: APEK's member directory explicitly states 570 listed members across 64 paginated pages, each with its own detail URL. This is by a wide margin the largest single enumeration found in this cell and the definitive map of the Czech e-commerce merchant and vendor base — the demand side for acquiring, payment gateways, BNPL and POS services. Each member detail page is a stable per-company URL, making the directory usable as a persistent company registry, not just a list.
candidates.legal_status: public website; contains business contact data — handle per GDPR, avoid harvesting personal contact details

Paginate via ?strana=1..64 (alphabetical or newest sort available), collect /seznam-clenu/<slug> detail URLs, then fetch each. Roughly 634 requests for a full sweep; throttle politely. Re-run quarterly and diff to detect joiners/leavers. English locale at /en.

Sourced from APEK plus Heureka. This is the best free demand-side payments-mix dataset for CZ and complements SBK's issuer-side card statistics from the opposite direction. Note the site cites 'more than 650' APEK members versus 570 listed on the directory — reconcile before quoting either figure.

candidates.source_name: Asociace českých stavebních spořitelen (AČSS)
candidates.why_relevant: Snowballed extension to the cell: the association of Czech building societies (stavební spořitelny), all of which are bank subsidiaries of the major groups (Modrá pyramida/KB, ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna, Stavební spořitelna ČS). Site carries 'Členové AČSS', 'Orgány AČSS', a 'Čísla a grafy' statistics section, a 'Novináři a odborníci' press area, legislation tracking and a terminology glossary. Building-society deposits and loans are a material and separately-regulated slice of Czech retail banking that the ČBA roster alone under-represents. Note acss.cz redirects to stavebnisporitelny.cz.
candidates.legal_status: public website
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Static HTML parse; homepage rendered fully to a plain client. Harvest 'Členové AČSS' for the roster, 'Čísla a grafy' for the statistics series and 'Novináři a odborníci' for the press feed. Also produces a video series ('Stavební spořitelny ve 21. století') whose guests identify sector executives. Quarterly.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowball — extended the cell beyond its six named associations to adjacent Czech banking-sector bodies, then verified by direct fetch

candidates.source_name: Česká asociace společností finančního poradenství a zprostředkování (ČASF)
candidates.why_relevant: Snowballed extension: the association of Czech financial advisory and intermediation companies — the distribution layer through which a large share of Czech mortgages, consumer credit and investment products is actually sold. Site carries 'Členské společnosti' (member companies), 'Finančně poradenský trh' (market data on the advisory sector), an ethics committee, and a media section. Member of FECIF at European level. Important for understanding origination channels that banks depend on but do not own. Note usfcr.cz redirects here, indicating an earlier identity (USF ČR) — useful for historical archive searches.
candidates.legal_status: public website
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Static HTML parse (WordPress); harvest 'Členské společnosti' and 'Finančně poradenský trh'. Check the Wayback Machine under usfcr.cz for the pre-rebrand archive when reconstructing historical member rosters. Quarterly.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowball to adjacent Czech financial-sector associations, verified by direct fetch; discovered the usfcr.cz -> casfpz.cz rebrand redirect in the process
local_language_terms_used: Česká asociace společností finančního poradenství a zprostředkování

candidates.source_name: Česká asociace pojišťoven (ČAP)
candidates.why_relevant: The Czech insurance association, relevant to this cell because bancassurance is a significant fee-income line for every large Czech bank and most banking groups own or distribute for an insurer. Its member registry and statistics would complete the financial-sector association map. Recorded here as a HYPOTHESIS: the connection was reset on fetch, which typically indicates bot defence rather than a dead site — liveness must be confirmed by the deterministic verification pass.
candidates.access_status: unverified — TCP connection reset during fetch
candidates.legal_status: presumed public website; not confirmed
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Retry with a full browser user-agent and TLS fingerprint, or a headless browser, before drawing any conclusion. Do not record as dead on this single failure.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowball to adjacent Czech financial-sector associations
candidates.observed_blocker: curl error 56: Recv failure: Connection reset by peer (HTTP code 000). Treated as bot-defended-but-probably-live, NOT as dead.

candidates.source_name: ČEFTAS Visualbook — association brand and identity assets

Marginal for market intelligence, but it confirms the ČEFTAS acronym and the association's Czech/Slovak dual-market positioning, and it is the kind of asset that dates rebrands — useful when reconciling historical references to the association under different names.

negative_findings.description: The WebSearch tool returned 'this session has used its web search budget (200 of 200 WebSearch calls)' on the very first query attempt, so no search-engine query — Czech or English — could be executed during this cell.
negative_findings.result_summary: All discovery was performed instead by direct HTTP fetch of candidate association domains, robots.txt/sitemap.xml enumeration, and recursive link-graph snowballing. This worked well for the six named associations (all six located and mapped) but eliminated the long-tail discovery path that would surface smaller or newer associations whose domains cannot be guessed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Coverage of the six seeded associations is thorough and evidence-backed, but the cell cannot claim completeness for Czech financial-sector associations generally. Any association without a guessable domain and without an inbound link from the ones crawled is invisible to this pass.

negative_findings.description: The Czech Fintech Association's official press release category at https://czechfintech.cz/category/tiskove-zpravy/ appears abandoned.
negative_findings.result_summary: The newest items retrieved are dated Kvě (May) 2022 and Bře (March) 2022 — the latter announcing Miroslav Lukeš and Ondřej Machač taking over the association's leadership. Meanwhile the same site's /clanky/ stream carries items dated 14-20 August 2026, so the site is live; only this category is dormant.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Anyone monitoring ČEFTAS via the obvious 'tiskové zprávy' URL would wrongly conclude the association is inactive, and would miss four years of activity. Monitoring must target /clanky/ and /udalosti/ instead, or the WordPress /feed/.

negative_findings.description: Member rosters at three of the six target associations are not present in server-rendered HTML.
negative_findings.result_summary: ČLFA /o-nas/clenske-spolecnosti returned 9,253 bytes of navigation and breadcrumb with zero company names; czechfintech.cz /clenove/ returned 274,188 bytes containing the headings 'Řádní členové' and 'Přidružení členové' but no member names (logo-image rendering); AKAT /Clenove-asociace returned 37,722 bytes with the same headings and no names. By contrast ČBA /o-nas/clenove and APEK /seznam-clenu rendered their full rosters in plain HTML.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Three of the cell's most valuable enumerations require headless-browser collection rather than simple HTTP, which changes the cost and fragility profile of the collection pipeline. The ČEFTAS case may have a cheaper workaround via its exposed WordPress REST API at /wp-json/wp/v2/.

negative_findings.description: ČBA's robots.txt disallows the storage path that appears to hold its annual report PDFs.
negative_findings.result_summary: https://www.cbaonline.cz/robots.txt contains 'Disallow: /api/', 'Disallow: /cba_online/' and 'Disallow: /journal_files_storage/'. The /o-nas/vyrocni-zpravy index renders 16 dated rows (2011 through 2026-05-26) with 'Zobrazit PDF' controls, but a static fetch of that page yielded no .pdf hrefs at all — the links are injected client-side and resolve into the disallowed storage area.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated harvesting of ČBA annual reports would breach the site's stated crawler policy. The compliant routes are manual retrieval, or a direct request to the ČBA press office. This is a policy constraint, not a technical one, and should be flagged to whoever configures the collector.

negative_findings.description: ČBA's main site is largely client-rendered, hiding most of its content from plain HTTP clients.
negative_findings.result_summary: https://www.cbaonline.cz/ returned 55,021 bytes but only 7 navigable links, and topic pages such as /stranky/pro-media, /stranky/pruzkumy-a-indexy and /stranky/prognozy returned nothing but the page title and nav chrome. Two independent WebFetch attempts on the homepage and /o-nas both reported that member, annual-report and press-release links were absent. The content was only recoverable via robots.txt -> sitemap.xml, which exposed 2,838 URLs including all 28 structural /stranky/ and /o-nas/ pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive crawler would grade ČBA — the single most important association in this cell — as a near-empty site. The sitemap-first approach should be the documented default for this domain, and is a transferable technique for other JS-heavy Czech association sites.

negative_findings.description: Česká asociace pojišťoven (cap.cz) could not be fetched.
negative_findings.result_summary: curl returned error 56 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' with HTTP code 000 — the connection was reset mid-response rather than refused or 404'd.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This pattern is characteristic of bot defence (TLS-fingerprint or user-agent filtering) on a live site, not of a dead host. Per the run's hard rules this is recorded as a hypothesis requiring the deterministic verification pass; it must not be marked dead. ČAP matters because bancassurance is a material fee-income line for Czech banks.

negative_findings.description: AKAT's 'Monitoring trhu' section is dormant despite the rest of the site being current.
negative_findings.result_summary: The newest item on https://www.akatcr.cz/Asociace-AKAT/Monitoring-trhu is a February 2019 TV interview with Jana Brodani about mutual fund investing. AKAT's press release and annual report sections are by contrast current to August 2026.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The section name promises exactly what a market-intelligence collector wants and delivers seven-year-old content. The live equivalents are /Zverejnena-data and /Dokumenty/Tiskova-zprava-AKAT; the collector configuration should skip Monitoring trhu.

negative_findings.description: APEK states two different member counts on two of its own properties.
negative_findings.result_summary: https://www.apek.cz/seznam-clenu states 'Celkem je vylistováno 570 členů' across 64 pages, while https://data.apek.cz/ describes APEK as a 'sdružení více než 650 podnikatelů' (association of more than 650 entrepreneurs).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The figures differ by roughly 14 percent. Either the data site is stale, or the directory excludes some membership class. Any headline citing APEK membership size must state which source and date it came from; the directory count is the defensible one because it is enumerable.

negative_findings.description: No Czech crypto-asset or digital-asset industry association was located in this cell.
negative_findings.result_summary: With WebSearch unavailable, no crypto-industry association domain could be discovered, and none of the six seeded associations linked to one. The nearest observed signal was editorial coverage of a euro stablecoin on the ČEFTAS /clanky/ stream — topical interest without an identified representative body.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: MiCA implementation makes crypto-asset service providers a live competitive and regulatory topic for Czech banks and payment firms. If a Czech CASP association exists, it is an unmapped pointer source. No URL is asserted here because none was found — guessing one would be fabrication.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Czech association of non-bank payment institutions or payment service providers was identified.
negative_findings.result_summary: Non-bank acquirers and PSPs do appear in Czech industry data — SBK's statistics contributor list names ComGate Payments, EVO Payments, Global Payments, Nexi, Euronet, KB Smart Pay, Twisto Payments and Direct Fidoo Payments — but they surface as data contributors to SBK, not as members of any PSP-specific trade body found in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It is plausible that no such Czech association exists and that SBK plus ČEFTAS jointly occupy that representational space. That is itself a useful structural finding: for Czech non-bank payments actors, SBK's contributor roster is the best available enumeration and should be treated as the primary registry for that segment.

negative_findings.description: Two collection-relevant encoding and URL hazards were observed that will silently corrupt a naive collector.
negative_findings.result_summary: First, the SBK and CardMag sites are legacy hand-built pages served in a Czech single-byte encoding — extracted text loses all diacritics under a UTF-8 assumption ('Sdružení' rendered as 'Sdruen', 'platebních karet' as 'platebnch karet'). Second, AKAT's DNN platform encodes Czech characters as decimal HTML entities inside URL slugs, e.g. '/Dokumenty/Vyrocni-zpravy/v253rocn237-zpr225va-20232024' for 'výroční zpráva'. Third, several SBK homepage hrefs are malformed, missing the slash after the host (e.g. 'http://aktuality.bankovnikarty.czTZ_MasterCard_18-08-2026.pdf').
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Each hazard produces silent failures rather than errors: mangled Czech entity names that will not match any actor map, unmatched URL patterns, and 'dead link' false positives on SBK that are actually authoring typos. All three need explicit handling in the collector.

coverage_gaps.description: Zero search-engine queries were executable in this cell because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before the first call. Discovery relied entirely on domain guessing plus link-graph snowballing.

Specifically hunt for associations with no inbound link from the six seeded bodies.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language mirrors were identified but not systematically enumerated or compared against their Czech originals.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Sweep the confirmed English endpoints — cbaonline.cz/about-us/members, cbamonitor.cz/en, apek.cz/en, czechfintech.cz/en/, clfa.cz/o-nas/annual-report and the ČLFA 'Quarterly and yearly results...' statistics page — and diff them against the Czech versions. Czech association sites routinely publish less in English and with a lag, so establish per-source whether the English mirror is complete, partial or stale before any English-only collection is configured.

coverage_gaps.description: Member-only tiers were identified at three associations but their contents remain uncharacterised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Document what sits behind SBK's data.bankovnikarty.cz/secure/ area, ČLFA's /pro-cleny section, AKAT's Registrace/Přihlásit login and APEK's komunita.apek.cz, by asking each association's press office directly rather than probing. Then decide whether any warrants paid membership. For komunita.apek.cz specifically, first test Discourse's public .json endpoints — the empty body observed is an SPA artefact and is not by itself evidence of a gate.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull archived captures of the ČBA, ČLFA, AKAT and APEK member pages from the Wayback Machine to build a longitudinal entry/exit series, and in particular capture usfcr.cz before its rebrand to casfpz.cz and acss.cz before its move to stavebnisporitelny.cz. SBK's dated contributor-exclusion notes already provide a partial 2017-2024 exit log for the cards market and should be the template for what to reconstruct elsewhere.

coverage_gaps.description: Insurance and crypto-asset representation in the Czech financial-sector association map is unresolved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm ČAP (cap.cz) liveness with a browser-grade client and map its member registry and statistics, given bancassurance's weight in Czech bank fee income. Separately, establish whether a Czech crypto-asset service provider association exists under MiCA — if none does, record that absence explicitly so downstream cells do not keep searching for it.

coverage_gaps.description: Association working groups, committees and named officeholders were located but not harvested, leaving the people layer of the actor map empty.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest ČBA /o-nas/komise-pracovni-skupiny and /o-nas/organy, ČLFA /o-nas/organy-clfa and /o-nas/lide---vedeni-clfa, AKAT /Asociace-AKAT/Organy-asociace, AČSS 'Orgány AČSS' and the ČEFTAS board and FinTech Ambassador lists. Committee membership reveals which bank owns which regulatory or technical agenda, and officeholder names are the highest-yield search keys for finding executive statements that never appear in formal disclosures. Pair this with an annual sweep of the Card Forum / Card Session / Prague Payments Week / Acquiring Day speaker lists.

coverage_gaps.description: No URL in this slice has been confirmed reachable by an independent verification pass, and several were reached only via redirects or non-obvious entry points.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Route every candidate URL through the deterministic liveness check, paying particular attention to: bankovnikarty.cz and cardmag.cz (root serves only a META-refresh shim — verify the /pages/... targets, not the root), acss.cz (redirects to stavebnisporitelny.cz), usfcr.cz (redirects to casfpz.cz), data.apek.cz (HTTP to HTTPS upgrade), and cap.cz (connection reset, expected to need a browser-grade client).

brief: All six seeded Czech sector associations were located and mapped, and the cell divides cleanly into two tiers. The high-value tier is ČBA (member roster of ~33 banks plus the separate ČBA Monitor statistics property carrying sector aggregates, the Hypomonitor mortgage series and the ČBA Prognóza), SBK (quarterly and annual card statistics spanning 2001-2026, plus a named contributor roster of 27 issuers and acquirers and a dated log of market exits that doubles as the best enumeration of non-bank Czech payments actors found anywhere in this cell), APEK (570 enumerable members across 64 static pages, plus the APEKdata portal with a dedicated online-payments section), and ČLFA (current quarterly leasing, consumer-credit and factoring statistics, an active press stream, and hosting for the otherwise-invisible Asociace factoringových společností ČR series). AKAT contributes a codified fund-data programme and quarterly aggregates including DIP uptake, while ČEFTAS is the weakest of the six as a data source — its official press category has been dormant since May 2022, though its article stream is current. Snowballing extended the cell to AČSS (building societies) and ČASF (advisory and intermediation distribution), and surfaced the SBK-adjacent trade press and conference circuit as a people-and-vendor index; ČAP remains unverified behind an apparent bot defence. Two collection caveats dominate: three of the six member rosters (ČLFA, ČEFTAS, AKAT) require headless-browser rendering, and ČBA is both JS-rendered — recoverable only through its 2,838-URL sitemap — and has its annual-report PDF store placed off-limits by robots.txt.
